title: Post-Enucleation Socket Syndrome (PESS): Clinical Mastery
summary: PESS represents the constellation of clinical signs resulting from volume deficiency in the anophthalmic socket following enucleation. Achieving long-term aesthetic and functional success requires a systematic approach to orbital volume restoration and secondary corrective surgery.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: PESS is characterized by a specific triad of signs: superior sulcus deepening, upper eyelid ptosis, and lower eyelid laxity with enophthalmos. Pathophysiology is rooted in the loss of orbital volume (the globe, plus the surgical removal of surrounding fascia and potential atrophy of fat), leading to a mechanical retraction of the superior levator complex and lack of support for the ocular prosthesis.

sections.title: Key Clinical Features
content: Deepening of the superior conjunctival sulcus
Blepharoptosis (upper lid droop due to loss of prosthesis support)
Discharge or poor motility of the implant/prosthesis

sections.title: Etiology: Factors Leading to Volume Loss

rows: Usually proptosis, but can present with asymmetric ptosis

sections.title: Surgical Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Evaluation of implant motility and size (Imaging/USG)
Step 2: Replacement of orbital implant (secondary orbital implant exchange)
Step 3: Volume augmentation via dermis-fat graft or porous hydroxyapatite sphere
Step 5: Lower lid tightening (lateral tarsal strip procedure)

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Investigate
content: Sudden increase in discharge (suspect giant papillary conjunctivitis or infection)

content.explanation: D: Deep Superior Sulcus; P: Ptosis (Upper lid); L: Lower lid laxity/ectropion.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: Primary prevention: Use the largest spherical implant that allows for conjunctival closure without tension.
Porous implants (e.g., Medpor, Hydroxyapatite) reduce long-term migration.
Always assess the status of the fornices before planning volume correction.
Consider fat grafting if the deep superior sulcus is the primary complaint.
